tools.image-palette.guide.whatIs.title: What Is Color Extraction?
tools.image-palette.guide.whatIs.body.0: Color extraction (palette extraction) automatically analyzes the most representative colors in an image and turns them into a palette.
tools.image-palette.guide.whatIs.body.1: It's commonly used for brand color inspiration, web design picking, and asset style analysis — a quick way to capture the color mood of any image.
tools.image-palette.guide.howTo.title: How to Extract a Color Palette
tools.image-palette.guide.howTo.intro: Three steps to extract an image's dominant colors:

tools.image-phash.metadata.title: Image Perceptual Hash - Compute pHash Online
tools.image-phash.metadata.description: Free online tool to compute the perceptual hash (pHash) of an image. The 64-bit hash is ideal for similar-image comparison and deduplication.
tools.image-phash.title: Image Perceptual Hash (pHash)
tools.image-phash.description: Compute the perceptual hash (pHash) of an image. pHash compresses image content into a 64-bit fingerprint, and similar images produce similar hashes — ideal for duplicate detection and similarity comparison.
tools.image-phash.faqs.0.question: What is a perceptual hash (pHash)?
tools.image-phash.faqs.0.answer: A perceptual hash is a content-aware image fingerprint: the image is shrunk and converted to grayscale, DCT is applied to extract low-frequency features, and a 64-bit hash is produced. Similar images get similar hashes.
tools.image-phash.faqs.1.question: How is pHash different from a regular hash?
tools.image-phash.faqs.1.answer: Regular hashes like MD5 or SHA are extremely sensitive — changing a single pixel changes the result completely. pHash focuses on the image's overall structure, so recompression, resizing, or slight color tweaks barely affect it.
tools.image-phash.faqs.2.question: How do I use the hash to tell if two images are similar?
tools.image-phash.faqs.2.answer: Compute the Hamming distance between the two hashes (the number of differing bits). The smaller the distance, the more similar — generally under 10-12 bits means highly similar.
tools.image-phash.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
tools.image-phash.faqs.3.answer: No. All computation happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.

tools.image-phash.guide.whatIs.title: What Is a Perceptual Hash?
tools.image-phash.guide.whatIs.body.0: A perceptual hash squeezes an image into a fixed-length fingerprint (64 bits here) while ensuring that visually similar images get similar fingerprints.
tools.image-phash.guide.whatIs.body.1: It works by extracting low-frequency features in the frequency domain with DCT, ignoring compression, resizing, and slight color shifts that don't affect how we perceive the image.
tools.image-phash.guide.howTo.title: How to Compute an Image Perceptual Hash
tools.image-phash.guide.howTo.intro: Three steps to compute the pHash of your image:
tools.image-phash.guide.howTo.items.0: Upload a local image (PNG, JPG, WEBP, or BMP supported).
tools.image-phash.guide.howTo.items.1: Click Compute Hash to generate the 64-bit hash value.
tools.image-phash.guide.howTo.items.2: Copy the HEX or binary result for programmatic comparison or archiving.
tools.image-phash.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.image-phash.guide.tips.items.0: Different compression or resized versions of the same image produce nearly identical hashes.
tools.image-phash.guide.tips.items.1: A Hamming distance under 10-12 bits indicates similar images.
tools.image-phash.guide.tips.items.2: Pair this tool with Duplicate Image Finder to deduplicate images in bulk.
tools.image-compare.metadata.title: Image Compare - Compare Two Images Online
tools.image-compare.metadata.description: Free online tool to compare two images: see the difference percentage at a glance and generate a red-highlighted difference map.
tools.image-compare.title: Image Compare
tools.image-compare.description: Upload two images, compare them pixel by pixel, and get a difference ratio plus a red-highlighted difference map — a quick way to pinpoint exactly what changed.
tools.image-compare.faqs.0.question: How is the difference ratio calculated?
tools.image-compare.faqs.0.answer: The second image is resized to match the first, then the two are compared pixel by pixel. Pixels whose color difference exceeds a threshold are counted as different, and their share of the total is the difference ratio.
tools.image-compare.faqs.1.question: What does red mean in the difference map?
tools.image-compare.faqs.1.answer: Red highlights mark the areas where the two images differ. Everything else is dimmed so you can spot every difference at a glance.
tools.image-compare.faqs.2.question: Can I compare images of different sizes?
tools.image-compare.faqs.2.answer: Yes. The tool automatically resizes the second image to match the first before comparing pixel by pixel.
tools.image-compare.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
tools.image-compare.faqs.3.answer: No. All comparison happens locally in your browser — your images never leave your device.

tools.image-compare.guide.whatIs.title: What Is Image Comparison?
tools.image-compare.guide.whatIs.body.0: The Image Compare tool analyzes two images pixel by pixel, computes an overall difference ratio, and highlights differing regions in red while dimming the identical parts.
tools.image-compare.guide.whatIs.body.1: It's commonly used to verify whether an image was modified, check design-versus-implementation gaps, and compare screenshots of different versions.
tools.image-compare.guide.howTo.title: How to Compare Two Images
tools.image-compare.guide.howTo.intro: Three steps to compare two images:
tools.image-compare.guide.howTo.items.0: Upload image A and image B in the two areas above (PNG, JPG, WEBP, or BMP supported).
tools.image-compare.guide.howTo.items.1: Click Compare to get the difference ratio and difference map.
tools.image-compare.guide.howTo.items.2: To keep the result, click Download Diff to save the comparison output.
tools.image-compare.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.image-compare.guide.tips.items.0: Using same-size images of the same content gives the clearest comparison.
tools.image-compare.guide.tips.items.1: A lower difference ratio means the two images are closer to identical.
tools.image-compare.guide.tips.items.2: To quickly check whether two images show the same content, run the Image Perceptual Hash tool first.
tools.duplicate-finder.metadata.title: Duplicate Image Finder - Detect Similar Images Online
tools.duplicate-finder.metadata.descript: Free online tool to batch detect duplicate or similar images. Groups them automatically with perceptual hashing to help you clean up duplicates.
tools.duplicate-finder.title: Duplicate Image Finder
tools.duplicate-finder.description: Upload multiple images at once. Each image gets a perceptual hash, and duplicates or highly similar images are grouped automatically — perfect for reclaiming disk space.
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.0.question: How are duplicate images detected?
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.0.answer: Every image is hashed with a perceptual hash (pHash). Images whose Hamming distance is small enough (similar enough) are automatically grouped together.
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.1.question: Can it detect modified images?
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.1.answer: Yes. Perceptual hashes are insensitive to resizing, compression, and slight color adjustments, so recompressed or resized copies are recognized too.
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.2.question: How many images can I upload at once?
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.2.answer: Up to 20 images at a time. Need to check more? Just run the detection in batches.
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
tools.duplicate-finder.faqs.3.answer: No. All detection happens locally in your browser — your images never leave your device.
tools.duplicate-finder.upload.drop: Drop multiple images or click to upload
tools.duplicate-finder.upload.formats: PNG, JPG, WEBP, BMP, up to 20 images
tools.duplicate-finder.labels.none: No duplicate or similar images found.

tools.duplicate-finder.guide.whatIs.body: Duplicate image detection generates a perceptual hash fingerprint for every image, compares the fingerprints pairwise with Hamming distance, and groups highly similar images together.
It's far more reliable than comparing file sizes or names — even copies with different names or dimensions are caught as long as the content matches.
tools.duplicate-finder.guide.howTo.title: How to Find Duplicate Images
tools.duplicate-finder.guide.howTo.intro: Three steps to find duplicate images:
tools.duplicate-finder.guide.howTo.items: Drag in or select multiple images (up to 20 at once; PNG, JPG, WEBP, or BMP supported).
Click Find Duplicates to start scanning — each image's hash is computed automatically.
Review the duplicate groups and similarity scores, then delete the copies you don't need.
tools.duplicate-finder.guide.tips.title: Tips
Images with a similarity above roughly 80% are grouped together.
Images in the same group may not be pixel-identical — preview before deleting.
Great for cleaning up downloaded assets, photo backups, and other duplicated content.
tools.rgb-channel-split.metadata.title: RGB Channel Split - Separate Image Channels Online
tools.rgb-channel-split.metadata.descrip: Free online tool to split an image into red, green, and blue channels. View and download each channel separately.
tools.rgb-channel-split.title: RGB Channel Split
tools.rgb-channel-split.description: Split an image into three independent red, green, and blue channels shown side by side. Each channel keeps only the brightness of its own color — great for learning color theory or creating channel assets.
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.0.question: What is an RGB channel?
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.0.answer: An RGB image is made of red, green, and blue color channels layered together. Each channel records the brightness of its own color, and the three combined produce the final displayed color.
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.1.question: What do the separated channel images look like?
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.1.answer: The red channel image keeps only red brightness information (the picture appears in red tones), and the green and blue channels work the same way. The brighter a channel, the stronger that color is in that area.
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.2.question: What is channel splitting used for?
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.2.answer: It's commonly used to learn color theory, create channel assets, diagnose color casts, and for color separation in professional print workflows.
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
tools.rgb-channel-split.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.
tools.rgb-channel-split.upload.drop: Drop an image or click to upload
tools.rgb-channel-split.errors.process: Failed to split the channels. Please try again.
tools.rgb-channel-split.guide.whatIs.bod: RGB channel splitting breaks a color image into three independent red, green, and blue images, each retaining only the brightness information of its own channel.
It's a fundamental operation for understanding digital color, and an important step in color separation and channel compositing workflows.
tools.rgb-channel-split.guide.howTo.intr: Three steps to split the RGB channels:
tools.rgb-channel-split.guide.howTo.item: Upload a local image (PNG, JPG, WEBP, or BMP supported).
Click Split Channels to generate the original plus the red, green, and blue channel images.
Click Download on any channel to save that single-channel image.
tools.rgb-channel-split.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.rgb-channel-split.guide.tips.items: The brighter a channel, the stronger that color is in that area.
If one channel looks overly bright or dark, it can help you diagnose a color cast.
Pair this with the Image Histogram tool to inspect the brightness distribution of each channel.
tools.image-web-optimizer.metadata.title: Web Image Optimizer - Compress Images Online
tools.image-web-optimizer.metadata.descr: Free online batch image compression with WebP, JPEG, and PNG conversion to reduce file size and speed up your web pages.
tools.image-web-optimizer.title: Web Image Optimizer
tools.image-web-optimizer.description: Compress images in bulk and convert them to web-friendly formats (WebP, JPEG, PNG), with adjustable maximum width and compression quality to significantly reduce file size. All processing happens locally in your browser.
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.0.questio: Will the optimized images lose quality?
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.0.answer: You can control the compression strength with the quality slider. Higher quality means less visible loss but larger files; lower quality produces smaller files with more visible loss.
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.1.answer: At the same visual quality, WebP is usually smaller than JPEG, which makes it great for websites. JPEG has the broadest compatibility and is a safe choice when wide support is needed.
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.2.questio: Can I optimize multiple images at once?
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.2.answer: Yes. You can upload up to 10 images at a time. After optimizing, you can download them individually or package them all into a ZIP file.
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.3.questio: Are my images uploaded to a server?
tools.image-web-optimizer.faqs.3.answer: No. All compression and format conversion happens locally in your browser — your images never leave your device.

tools.image-web-optimizer.guide.whatIs.b: Web image optimization reduces file size through compression, resizing, and format conversion, which speeds up page loading and saves bandwidth.
A common approach is to output WebP and choose an appropriate compression quality to balance quality against file size.
tools.image-web-optimizer.guide.howTo.in: Optimize your images in three steps:
tools.image-web-optimizer.guide.howTo.it: Upload images (up to 10) in PNG, JPG, WEBP, or BMP format.
Set the maximum width, quality, and output format (WebP/JPEG/PNG).
Click Optimize All, then download images individually or as a ZIP.
tools.image-web-optimizer.guide.tips.ite: For web background images, output WebP and lower the quality a bit.
For icons or images that need transparency, choose PNG or WebP.
Compare the old and new file sizes before optimizing to avoid over-compressing.
tools.batch-rename.metadata.title: Batch Rename - Rename Files Online
tools.batch-rename.metadata.description: Free online batch file renaming with rule chains: find & replace, regex, sequence numbering, case conversion. Preview new names in real time and download as ZIP.
tools.batch-rename.title: Batch Rename
tools.batch-rename.description: Batch rename any type of files with configurable rules. Combine find & replace, regex, sequence numbering, case conversion, insert and cleanup rules into a chain, preview every new name in real time, then download the renamed files as a ZIP or copy the renaming list.
tools.batch-rename.faqs.0.question: What are rename rules?
tools.batch-rename.faqs.0.answer: Rules are the building blocks of renaming. You can add find & replace, regex, sequence numbering, case conversion, insert and cleanup rules, combine them in any order, and the chain runs from top to bottom on every file name.
tools.batch-rename.faqs.1.question: Will this modify my local files?
tools.batch-rename.faqs.1.answer: No. The tool only generates new names and packages copies for download — your original files are never modified.
tools.batch-rename.faqs.2.question: How many files can I rename at once?
tools.batch-rename.faqs.2.answer: You can upload up to 1000 files of any type at a time, and the file name list updates in real time.
tools.batch-rename.faqs.3.question: How do I avoid duplicate names?
tools.batch-rename.faqs.3.answer: Conflicts are detected automatically and highlighted in the preview. Use the Fix Conflicts button to automatically append (1), (2) and so on.
tools.batch-rename.faqs.4.question: Are the extensions preserved?
tools.batch-rename.faqs.4.answer: By default the rules apply to the file name only and the extension is preserved. You can switch the scope to Extension or Full name to apply rules there instead.
